entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Bluebeard, a French folktale figure created by Charles Perrault, has been an enduring cultural icon since the 17th century. In Perrault's 1697 collection of tales, 'Histoires ou Contes du Temps Passé,' Bluebeard is presented as a mysterious and sinister husband who murders his wives and hides their bodies in a secret chamber.

The story of Bluebeard has been translated into numerous languages and has influenced various artistic and literary works. It has also been adapted into films, stage productions, and opera.

Despite its dark origins, the tale of Bluebeard has become a symbol of the dangers of unchecked male power and the importance of female agency. Perrault's work has had a lasting impact on Western folklore and continues to be widely studied by scholars today.

A 2019 study found that the story of Bluebeard has been referenced in over 1,000 literary works, including those by authors such as Jane Austen and Edgar Allan Poe.
